title: 1988 AHSME Problem 14
statement: For any real number \(a\) and positive integer \(k,\) define \[ \binom ak= \frac{\begin{gathered} a(a-1)(a-2)\cdots\\ {}\cdot(a-(k-1)) \end{gathered}} {\begin{gathered} k(k-1)(k-2)\cdots\\ {}\cdot(2)(1) \end{gathered}}. \] What is \[\binom{-\frac12}{100}\div\binom{\frac12}{100}\ ?\]

solutions.text:
After canceling \(100!,\) the numerator factors have magnitudes \(1,3,\ldots,199,\) while the denominator factors have magnitudes \(1,1,3,\ldots,197.\) All common odd factors cancel, leaving magnitude \(199.\) The numerator has \(100\) negative factors and the denominator has \(99,\) so the quotient is \(-199.\)

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: Write the remaining factors as consecutive odd integers and look for telescoping cancellation
